title: SLCO1B1 variants and statin-induced myopathy--a genomewide study
authors: SEARCH Collaborative Group, Link E, Parish S, Armitage J, Bowman L, Heath S, et al.
population: Genomewide association study of 85 participants with definite or incipient myopathy and 90 matched controls, all taking simvastatin 80 mg daily in the SEARCH trial of 12,064 survivors of myocardial infarction; replication in 16,664 genotyped participants of the Heart Protection Study taking simvastatin 40 mg daily
funder: Supported by the Medical Research Council, British Heart Foundation, National Health Service Genetic Knowledge Park, and Centre National de Génotypage. The SEARCH trial is funded by a research grant to the University of Oxford (Oxford, United Kingdom) from Merck. The Heart Protection Study was funded by grants from Merck, Roche Vitamins, the Medical Research Council, and the British Heart Foundation.
authorConflicts: No potential conflict of interest relevant to this article was reported. The paper states that the myopathy study was designed, analysed and interpreted by the writing committee; the SEARCH steering committee lists J. Tobert and T. Musliner as observers.
result: A single strong association of myopathy was found with rs4363657 in SLCO1B1 (P = 4 x 10^-9), in near-complete linkage disequilibrium (r2 = 0.97) with the non-synonymous rs4149056 (Val174Ala) in exon 6. The estimated population prevalence of the rs4149056 C allele was 15%. Odds ratio for myopathy 4.5 (95% CI 2.6 to 7.7) per C allele and 16.9 (4.7 to 61.1) for CC against TT. Estimated cumulative myopathy risk on simvastatin 80 mg daily: 18% with CC, about 3% with CT and 0.6% with TT; more than 60% of the myopathy cases were attributable to the C allele. In the Heart Protection Study on 40 mg daily the association was replicated with an odds ratio of 2.6 (1.3 to 5.0) per C allele.
